page: Amazon Web Services m7a.12xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and AMD EPYC 9R14 processors. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it provides 48 dedicated physical cores operating at 3.7 GHz with a 1:1 thread-to-core mapping. The system incorporates 192.0 GB of DDR5 memory clocked at 5 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The processor includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, alongside hardware support for AVX-512 extensions including VNNI and BF16, as well as AES and SHA cryptography instructions. There is no bundled local storage or integrated GPU, and network performance delivers a baseline bandwidth of 19 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong computational and memory performance across multi-threaded workloads. In stress-ng testing, multi-core CPU throughput reached 147,533.61 points, ranking in the top 10 percent of evaluated systems, complemented by a Geekbench multi-core score of 17,777.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 79,965.1. High-throughput memory testing recorded 196.87 GB/sec for uncached 256MB reads and 124.3 GB/sec for writes. Workload-specific benchmarks reflect these characteristics, achieving 115.33 million Redis SET operations per second, 45.84 GB/sec in static web serving throughput, and 50,421.0 points in Clang software compilation tests.

The absence of integrated local storage means instances depend entirely on network-attached storage architectures, introducing storage latency tradeoffs that must be managed over the 19 Gbps network baseline. While single-thread decompression and compression metrics remain moderate, the high core density and DDR5 bandwidth offer efficient resource scaling for parallel tasks. The instance provides strong qualitative cost efficiency for organizations requiring high core counts and DDR5 memory throughput without paying for accelerator hardware or local NVMe pools.

Given its hardware balance and high parallel compute capabilities, the m7a.12xlarge is suited for scalable enterprise web serving, distributed caching systems like Redis, relational database backends, automated CI/CD compilation pipelines, and CPU-based machine learning inference pipelines.
